sheets.title: AC with R only and RMS

cards.title: Alternating EMF and RMS value
cards.body: A coil rotating at angular speed \(\omega\) in a magnetic field generates \(E = E_0 \sin \omega t\). Its effective (RMS) value is \(E_0/\sqrt{2} = 0.707 E_0\), and half-cycle mean is \(2E_0/\pi\).

cards.title: RMS value of a sinusoidal current
cards.legend: \(T\) period, \(I_0\) peak current, \(I_{rms}\) root-mean-square current.

phases.name: Define
phases.why: mean of i² over a period

steps.note: RMS is the square root of the mean of i² over one period.
Put in i = I₀ sin ωt.

ask.q: Why do we average i² and not i?
options: The average of i over a cycle is zero
ask.why: Positive and negative halves cancel for i, but not for i².

steps.note: Use the half-angle form of sin².

ask.q: Which identity makes \(\sin^2\omega t\) easy to integrate?
ask.why: It turns the square into a constant plus a cosine.

steps.note: The cosine has equal positive and negative areas over a period; ∫1 dt = T.

ask.q: Why does the \(\cos 2\omega t\) term integrate to zero over one period?
options: It is positive as often as negative
ask.why: Equal positive and negative areas cancel.

steps.note: The T cancels.
About 0.707 I₀. For 230 V rms the peak is about 325 V.

cards.title: Circuit: resistor on AC
cards.body: An AC source drives a resistor. By Kirchhoff's loop law the EMF equals the drop across \(R\) at every instant: \(v = iR\).

cards.title: Purely resistive AC circuit
cards.body: When \(E = E_0 \sin \omega t\) is applied across a resistor \(R\), the current is \(I = I_0 \sin \omega t\) with \(I_0 = E_0/R\). Current and voltage are in phase.

cards.title: Pure resistor: current in phase with the EMF
cards.legend: \(V\) applied EMF, \(i\) current, \(R\) resistance, \(\omega\) angular frequency.

phases.name: Setup
phases.why: the generator EMF across a pure resistance

steps.note: The generator gives a sinusoidal EMF across a pure resistance.

ask.q: Across a pure resistor, which law links the instantaneous current to the instantaneous voltage?
ask.why: For a pure resistance the current at each instant is \(V/R\).

steps.note: Divide both sides by R to bring in Ohm's law.

ask.q: We divide both sides by \(R\). Why?
options: To get \(V/R\), which equals the current
ask.why: \(V/R\) is the current by Ohm's law.

steps.note: Replace V/R by the current i.
Same \(\sin\omega t\): current and EMF rise and fall together, phase difference 0.

ask.q: What is the phase difference between \(i\) and \(V\) in a pure resistor?
ask.why: Both are proportional to \(\sin\omega t\), so they are in phase.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: What is the form factor of a sinusoidal alternating current?
cards.why: Form factor is the ratio of RMS value to half-cycle mean value: \(0.707 E_0 / (0.637 E_0) = \pi/(2\sqrt{2}) \approx 1.11\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In a pure resistor connected to an AC source, what is the phase difference between voltage and current?
cards.why: i = (V₀/R) sin ωt has the same phase as V.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: A household supply is rated \(230\ \text{V}\) rms. What is its peak voltage?

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: Over one full cycle the average value of a sinusoidal current is ______, but its rms value is \(I_0/\sqrt{2}\).
cards.why: Positive and negative half-cycles cancel in the plain average.

cards.title: Purely inductive AC circuit
cards.body: Across a pure inductor \(L\), the induced EMF opposes current change. The current is \(I = I_0 \sin(\omega t - \pi/2)\), lagging behind the applied voltage by \(90^\circ\).

cards.title: Circuit: inductor on AC
cards.body: An ideal inductor across an AC source. The EMF balances the self-induced EMF: \(v = L\,di/dt\).
cards.label: Circuit

cards.title: Current in a pure inductor
cards.legend: \(E_0\) peak voltage, \(\omega\) angular frequency, \(L\) inductance, \(I\) current, \(I_0\) peak current.

phases.why: find current from rate of change

steps.note: Applied alternating voltage equals the magnitude of self-induced EMF.

ask.q: Across a pure inductor, the applied voltage has to balance
ask.why: An ideal inductor has no resistance.

steps.note: Isolate the rate of change of current \(dI/dt\).

ask.q: How do we obtain \(I(t)\) from \(dI/dt\)?
options: Integrate both sides with respect to \(t\)
ask.why: Integration with respect to time undoes the time derivative \(d/dt\).

steps.note: Integrating \(\sin(\omega t)\) gives \(-\cos(\omega t)/\omega\).

ask.q: To get \(I\) from \(dI/dt\) we
ask.why: Integration undoes differentiation.

steps.note: Rewrite \(-\cos(\omega t)\) to compare phase directly with \(\sin(\omega t)\).

ask.q: What does the factor \(E_0/(\omega L)\) represent?
ask.why: Since the maximum value of \(\sin(\omega t - \pi/2)\) is 1, \(E_0/(\omega L)\) is the peak current \(I_0\).

steps.note: Current lags behind the applied voltage by \(\pi/2\) radians.

cards.title: Purely capacitive AC circuit
cards.body: Across a pure capacitor \(C\), charge is \(q = CE\) and current is \(I = dq/dt = I_0 \sin(\omega t + \pi/2)\). The current leads the applied voltage by \(90^\circ\).

cards.body: An ideal capacitor across an AC source. The EMF equals the capacitor voltage: \(v = q/C\), and \(i = dq/dt\).

cards.title: Pure capacitor: current leads the EMF by π/2
cards.legend: \(q\) charge on the plates, \(C\) capacitance, \(V\) applied EMF, \(X_C\) capacitive reactance.

steps.note: The plates hold charge q = CV, and V = V₀ sin ωt.

ask.q: What links the charge on a capacitor to its voltage?
ask.why: Capacitance is charge per volt, so \(q = CV\).

steps.note: Current is the rate of flow of charge, so differentiate q.

ask.q: Current in the circuit is the ______ of the charge on the plates.
ask.why: \(i = dq/dt\).

steps.note: Replace dq/dt by the current i.
A cosine is a sine shifted by π/2.

ask.q: Which identity turns \(\cos\omega t\) into a sine?
ask.why: Shifting a sine forward by a quarter cycle gives a cosine.

steps.note: 1/ωC acts like a resistance: the capacitive reactance. The current leads the EMF by π/2.

ask.q: A capacitor's reactance \(X_C = 1/\omega C\). As the frequency rises, \(X_C\)
ask.why: \(\omega\) is in the denominator, so \(X_C\) falls with frequency.

cards.label: Example
cards.title: Reactance at 50 Hz
cards.body: For a \(0.3\ \text{H}\) coil on India's \(50\ \text{Hz}\) grid, \(\omega = 100\pi\ \text{rad/s}\) and \(X_L = 94.2\ \Omega\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, what is the phase relationship between current and applied voltage?
options: Current and voltage are in phase
cards.why: Because \(I = C(dE/dt)\), differentiating \(\sin \omega t\) gives \(\cos \omega t = \sin(\omega t + \pi/2)\), so current leads by \(\pi/2\).

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: The opposition offered by an inductor or a capacitor to the flow of alternating current is called ______.
cards.why: Reactance \(X\) is the non-resistive opposition to AC from inductance (\(X_L = \omega L\)) or capacitance (\(X_C = 1/\omega C\)).

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: An inductor of inductance \(0.5\ \text{H}\) is connected to an AC source of angular frequency \(200\ \text{rad/s}\). Find its inductive reactance.
cards.why: Inductive reactance is \(X_L = \omega L = 200 \times 0.5 = 100\ \Omega\).

sheets.title: The j operator in AC circuits

cards.title: The j operator
cards.body: In AC circuit analysis, \(j = \sqrt{-1}\) so that \(j^2 = -1\) and \(1/j = -j\). Multiplying a phasor by \(j\) rotates it through \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise; \(-j\) rotates it \(90^\circ\) clockwise.
cards.art: <svg viewBox="0 0 260 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Phasor rotation by +j and -j in complex plane"><line x1="80" y1="90" x2="210" y2="90" class="lk" stroke-width="2.5"/><line x1="80" y1="90" x2="80" y2="20" class="hk" stroke-width="3"/><line x1="80" y1="90" x2="80" y2="160" class="lk" stroke-width="2.5"/><text x="215" y="95" font-size="14" class="t">E_R</text><text x="92" y="32" font-size="14" class="t">+j E_L</text><text x="92" y="158" font-size="14" class="t">-j E_C</text></svg>

cards.title: Complex voltage and current
cards.body: An alternating EMF \(E_0 \sin \omega t\) is the imaginary part of \(E = E_0 e^{j\omega t}\). A current lagging by \(\phi\) is the imaginary part of \(I = I_0 e^{j(\omega t - \phi)}\).
cards.tex: E = E_0 e^{j\omega t}, \quad I = I_0 e^{j(\omega t - \phi)}

cards.title: Complex impedance Z
cards.body: Since inductor voltage leads current by \(90^\circ\) and capacitor voltage lags by \(90^\circ\), their complex impedances are \(Z_L = j\omega L\) and \(Z_C = 1/(j\omega C) = -j/(\omega C)\).
cards.tex: Z = R + jX = R + j\left(\omega L - \frac{1}{\omega C}\right)

cards.title: Polar form and admittance
cards.body: Complex impedance \(Z = R + jX\) has magnitude \(|Z| = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2}\) and phase angle \(\phi = \tan^{-1}(X/R)\). The reciprocal \(Y = 1/Z\) is called admittance.

cards.title: Circuit: series LCR
cards.body: R, L and C in series with the source. Loop law: \(L\,di/dt + Ri + q/C = v\). The j operator turns this into algebra.
cards.label: Circuit

cards.title: Inductor in j notation: Z_L = jωL
cards.legend: \(j = \sqrt{-1}\), \(i\) complex current, \(v_L\) voltage across the inductor, \(L\) inductance.

phases.name: Setup
phases.why: write the current as a rotating phasor

steps.note: A sinusoidal current written as the rotating phasor I₀e^{jωt}.

ask.q: What does \(e^{j\omega t}\) represent in the complex plane?
options: A vector of length 1 rotating at angular speed ω
ask.why: Euler: e^{jωt} = cos ωt + j sin ωt.

steps.note: Differentiating e^{jωt} brings down a factor jω.

ask.q: What does \(d/dt\) do to \(e^{j\omega t}\)?
ask.why: \(\frac{d}{dt}e^{j\omega t} = j\omega e^{j\omega t}\).

steps.note: d/dt just multiplies the phasor by jω.
L di/dt is the voltage across the inductor.

ask.q: Which quantity is L di/dt?
ask.why: Faraday: the voltage across an ideal inductor is L di/dt.

steps.note: v_L = (jωL) i, so Z_L = jωL: magnitude ωL, and j means the voltage leads the current by 90°.

ask.q: Since \(j = e^{j\pi/2}\), the voltage across an inductor ______ the current.
ask.why: Multiplying by \(j\) rotates the phasor forward by 90°.

cards.title: Capacitor in j notation: Z_C = 1/(jωC)
cards.legend: \(v\) complex voltage across the capacitor, \(i\) current, \(C\) capacitance.

phases.name: Impedance
phases.why: solve for v in terms of i

steps.note: The capacitor voltage as a rotating phasor.
Differentiating e^{jωt} brings down jω.
d/dt multiplies the phasor by jω.
Multiply by C: C dv/dt is the capacitor current.

ask.q: The current into a capacitor is
ask.why: From q = Cv and i = dq/dt.

steps.note: Replace C dv/dt by i.
Solve for v.

ask.q: To get \(v\) alone from \(i = j\omega Cv\) we
ask.why: v is multiplied by jωC, so divide by it.

steps.note: Z_C = 1/(jωC).
Since 1/j = −j: Z_C = −j/ωC, so the voltage lags the current by 90°.

ask.q: \(1/j\) equals
ask.why: Multiply top and bottom by \(j\): \(1/j = j/j^2 = -j\).

cards.title: Series LCR current via j operator
cards.legend: \(Z\) total complex impedance, \(R\) resistance, \(L\) inductance, \(C\) capacitance, \(\phi\) phase angle.

phases.name: Polar Z
phases.why: write impedance as magnitude and phase

phases.name: Ohm's law
phases.why: divide complex EMF by complex impedance

steps.note: In series, complex impedances of \(R\), \(L\) and \(C\) add directly.

ask.q: How do we rewrite \(1/(j\omega C)\) to group the imaginary terms?
ask.why: Since \(j^2 = -1\), multiplying numerator and denominator by \(j\) gives \(1/j = -j\).

steps.note: Factor out \(j\) from the inductive and capacitive reactances.

ask.q: \(1/j\) equals
ask.why: 1/j = j/j² = −j.

steps.note: Convert rectangular impedance to polar form with \(|Z| = \sqrt{R^2 + (\omega L - 1/\omega C)^2}\).

ask.q: The magnitude of \(Z = R + jX\) is
ask.why: Pythagoras in the complex plane.

steps.note: Apply complex Ohm's law \(I = E/Z\) with \(E = E_0 e^{j\omega t}\).

ask.q: What happens to the phase factor \(e^{j\phi}\) in the denominator?
ask.why: Dividing exponentials subtracts their exponents: \(e^{j\omega t}/e^{j\phi} = e^{j(\omega t - \phi)}\).

steps.note: The imaginary part gives \(i = (E_0/|Z|)\sin(\omega t - \phi)\).

cards.label: Example
cards.title: Magnitude of complex Z
cards.body: A circuit with \(R = 30\ \Omega\), \(X_L = 80\ \Omega\) and \(X_C = 40\ \Omega\) has net reactance \(X = 40\ \Omega\) and impedance \(50\ \Omega\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In the j-operator representation of AC circuits, what is the complex impedance of a capacitor C?
cards.why: Capacitive impedance is \(Z_C = 1/(j\omega C)\). Since \(1/j = -j\), this equals \(-j/(\omega C)\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: Multiplying an alternating phasor by the operator \(-j\) corresponds to which geometric operation?
cards.why: Since \(+j = e^{j\pi/2}\) rotates a vector by \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise, \(-j = e^{-j\pi/2}\) rotates it by \(90^\circ\) clockwise.

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: The reciprocal of the impedance Z of an AC circuit is called ______.
cards.why: Admittance \(Y = 1/Z\) measures how easily an AC circuit allows current to flow.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: An AC circuit has complex impedance \(Z = 6 - j8\ \Omega\). What is the magnitude of its impedance?
cards.why: The magnitude is \(|Z| = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\ \Omega\).

cards.title: Series L-R circuit
cards.body: For inductance \(L\) and resistance \(R\) in series, \(Z = R + j\omega L\) and \(|Z| = \sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}\). Current lags behind voltage by \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(\omega L/R)\).

cards.title: Circuit: L and R in series
cards.body: A coil (or inductor plus resistor) in series with the source. Loop law: \(L\,di/dt + Ri = v\).
cards.label: Circuit

cards.title: Series L-R from the loop law
cards.legend: \(i\) current, \(I\) complex current amplitude, \(Z\) impedance, \(\phi\) phase angle.

phases.name: Loop law
phases.why: voltage drops add to the EMF

steps.note: Kirchhoff's loop law: the drops across L and R add up to the applied EMF.

ask.q: Kirchhoff's loop law says that around a closed loop the voltage drops
options: add up to the source EMF
ask.why: Energy conservation around the loop.

steps.tex: j\omega LIe^{j\omega t}+RIe^{j\omega t} = V_0e^{j\omega t}
steps.note: With i = Ie^{jωt}, di/dt gives jω.
The common factor e^{jωt} cancels.

ask.q: Why can \(e^{j\omega t}\) be cancelled?
options: It is common to every term
ask.why: Dividing both sides by a common factor is allowed.

steps.note: Take I out as a common factor.
Complex Ohm's law: I = V/Z with Z = R + jωL.

ask.q: Complex Ohm's law gives the current amplitude as
ask.why: I = V/Z.

steps.note: Write R + jωL = |Z|e^{jφ}: |Z| = √(R²+ω²L²), φ = tan⁻¹(ωL/R). The current lags the EMF by φ.

ask.q: The angle of \(R+j\omega L\) in the complex plane is
ask.why: Angle = tan⁻¹(imaginary/real).

cards.title: Series C-R circuit
cards.body: For capacitance \(C\) and resistance \(R\) in series, \(Z = R - j/(\omega C)\) and \(|Z| = \sqrt{R^2 + 1/(\omega C)^2}\). Current leads the applied voltage by \(\theta = \tan^{-1}[1/(\omega CR)]\).

cards.body: A capacitor and a resistor in series with the source. Loop law: \(Ri + q/C = v\).

cards.title: Series C-R from the loop law
cards.legend: \(i\) current, \(I\) complex amplitude, \(\phi\) phase angle by which the current leads the EMF.

phases.name: Loop law
phases.why: voltage drops add to the EMF

steps.note: Loop law: the drop across R plus the capacitor voltage q/C = (1/C)∫i dt equals the EMF.

ask.q: The voltage across a capacitor in terms of the current is
ask.why: q = ∫i dt and V = q/C.

steps.tex: RIe^{j\omega t}+\frac{1}{j\omega C}Ie^{j\omega t} = V_0e^{j\omega t}
steps.note: With i = Ie^{jωt}, ∫dt gives 1/jω.
The common factor e^{jωt} cancels.

ask.q: \(\int e^{j\omega t}\,dt\) equals
ask.why: Integration divides by jω.

steps.note: Take I out as a common factor.
Complex Ohm's law with Z = R + 1/(jωC).
Use 1/j = −j.

ask.q: In \(Z = R - j/\omega C\) the imaginary part is
ask.why: A capacitor contributes −j/ωC.

steps.note: R − j/ωC has angle −φ, so 1/Z has +φ: the current leads the EMF by φ.

ask.q: In a series C-R circuit the current ______ the EMF.
ask.why: The capacitor makes the circuit capacitive.

cards.label: Example
cards.title: L-R at 50 Hz
cards.body: \(R = 100\ \Omega\), \(L = 0.5\ \text{H}\), \(f = 50\ \text{Hz}\): the current lags the EMF by \(57.5^\circ\).

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: In a series R-C circuit, the alternating current ______ the applied EMF in phase.
cards.why: Because capacitive reactance makes the voltage lag behind the current, the current leads the applied EMF by \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(1/\omega CR)\).

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: A series L-R circuit has resistance \(30\ \Omega\) and inductive reactance \(30\ \Omega\). By how many degrees does the current lag behind the voltage?
cards.why: Since \(\tan\theta = X_L/R = 30/30 = 1\), the phase lag angle is \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In a series L-R circuit, what happens to the phase angle \(\phi\) as the frequency is increased?
cards.why: \(\tan\phi = \omega L/R\) grows with \(\omega\).

cards.title: Parallel L-C circuit
cards.body: With \(L\) and \(C\) in parallel across \(E = E_0 \sin \omega t\), the branch currents are \(180^\circ\) out of phase: \(I = E_0(\omega C - 1/\omega L)\cos \omega t\). At \(\omega C = 1/\omega L\), total current is zero.

cards.title: Circuit: L and C in parallel
cards.body: An inductor and a capacitor in parallel across the source. Both branches have the same voltage; the branch currents add: \(i = i_L + i_C\).
cards.label: Circuit

cards.title: Parallel LC current and resonance
cards.legend: \(I\) total line current, \(E_0\) peak voltage, \(\omega\) angular frequency, \(L\) inductance, \(C\) capacitance.

phases.name: Branch sum
phases.why: add inductor and capacitor branch currents

steps.tex: I = \frac{E_0}{\omega L}\sin(\omega t - \pi/2) + E_0 \omega C \sin(\omega t + \pi/2)
steps.note: Total current is \(I_L + I_C\), with \(I_L\) lagging and \(I_C\) leading by \(\pi/2\).

ask.q: In a parallel circuit the branch currents
options: add (as phasors) to give the line current
ask.why: Kirchhoff's current law.

steps.tex: I = -\frac{E_0}{\omega L}\cos(\omega t) + E_0 \omega C \cos(\omega t)
steps.note: The two branch currents are \(180^\circ\) out of phase with each other.

ask.q: \(\sin(\omega t-\pi/2)\) equals
ask.why: Shifting a sine back a quarter cycle gives −cos.

steps.note: Factor out \(E_0 \cos(\omega t)\) to see the net current amplitude.

ask.q: What condition makes the total line current \(I\) vanish at all times?
ask.why: When \(\omega C - 1/(\omega L) = 0\), the two branch currents cancel completely and \(I = 0\).

steps.note: At resonance, capacitive susceptance equals inductive susceptance.

ask.q: How do we isolate \(\omega^2\) from \(\omega C = 1/(\omega L)\)?
ask.why: Multiplying both sides by \(\omega / C\) gives \(\omega^2 = 1/(LC)\).

steps.note: Collect \(\omega^2\) on the left and \(LC\) on the right.

cards.label: Example
cards.title: Width of central maximum
cards.body: For \(\lambda = 500\ \text{nm}\) incident on a \(0.2\ \text{mm}\) slit with a screen at \(D = 3\ \text{m}\), the central maximum has linear width \(15\ \text{mm}\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In a single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern, what happens to the central maximum if the slit width b is halved?
options: The central maximum becomes a dark fringe
cards.why: Since the first minimum is at \(\sin\theta \approx \lambda/b\), halving the slit width \(b\) doubles the angular spread.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: What is the approximate ratio of the intensity of the first secondary maximum to that of the central maximum in a single-slit Fraunhofer pattern?
cards.why: The first secondary maximum occurs at \(\beta \approx 1.43\pi\), giving \(I/I_0 = [\sin(1.43\pi)/(1.43\pi)]^2 \approx 0.0496\) or \(4.96\%\).

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: In single-slit Fraunhofer diffraction, the non-central maxima occur at roots of the transcendental equation \(\tan\beta =\) ______.
cards.why: Setting \(dI/d\beta = 0\) gives \(\sin\beta(\beta - \tan\beta) = 0\), so maxima satisfy \(\tan\beta = \beta\).

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: Monochromatic light of wavelength \(600\ \text{nm}\) falls normally on a single slit of width \(0.3\ \text{mm}\). Find the angle of the first diffraction minimum in milliradians.
cards.why: For the first minimum, \(\theta \approx \lambda/b = (600 \times 10^{-9}) / (0.3 \times 10^{-3}) = 2 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{rad} = 2\ \text{mrad}\).

cards.body: Interference maxima occur at \(\gamma = n\pi\) or \(d\sin\theta = n\lambda\). Intensity vanishes at diffraction minima \(b\sin\theta = m\lambda\) and at interference minima \(d\sin\theta = (n + 1/2)\lambda\).

cards.label: Example
cards.title: Missing orders for d = 4b
cards.body: When slit separation \(d = 4b\), the 4th interference maximum falls on the 1st diffraction minimum, leaving \(n = 0, \pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 3\) (7 bright fringes) inside the central peak.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In a two-slit Fraunhofer diffraction experiment, each slit has width b and the separation between slit centres is d = 3b. Which interference orders are missing?
cards.why: Missing orders satisfy \(n = (d/b)m = 3m\) for \(m = \pm 1, \pm 2, \dots\), so \(n = \pm 3, \pm 6, \pm 9, \dots\) are absent.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In the double-slit Fraunhofer formula \(I = 4I_0 (\sin^2\beta/\beta^2)\cos^2\gamma\), what happens if the slit width b becomes extremely small (\(b \ll \lambda\))?
options: \(\sin^2\beta/\beta^2 \approx 1\) and the pattern reduces to Young's double-slit fringes
\(\cos^2\gamma \approx 1\) and the pattern reduces to a single-slit pattern
cards.why: When \(b \to 0\), \(\beta \to 0\) and \(\sin^2\beta/\beta^2 \to 1\) across the screen, leaving pure \(4I_0\cos^2\gamma\) Young's fringes.

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: An interference maximum that fails to appear because it coincides with a diffraction minimum is called a ______ order.
cards.why: When \(d\sin\theta = n\lambda\) and \(b\sin\theta = m\lambda\) hold at the same angle, the diffraction envelope is zero and order \(n\) is a missing order.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: In a double-slit diffraction setup, the slit width is \(0.1\ \text{mm}\) and the distance between slit centres is \(0.5\ \text{mm}\). What is the smallest positive interference order n that is missing?
cards.why: The first diffraction minimum (\(m = 1\)) suppresses interference order \(n = (d/b) \times 1 = 0.5 / 0.1 = 5\).

cards.title: N-slit intensity distribution
cards.body: For \(N\) parallel equidistant slits of width \(b\) and period \(d\), the intensity is \(I = I_0 \frac{\sin^2\beta}{\beta^2}\frac{\sin^2 N\gamma}{\sin^2\gamma}\), where \(\beta = \frac{\pi b\sin\theta}{\lambda}\) and \(\gamma = \frac{\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda}\).

cards.title: Principal maxima & minima
cards.body: Principal maxima occur when \(\gamma = m\pi\), giving the grating equation \(d\sin\theta = m\lambda\). Between two adjacent principal maxima lie \(N - 1\) secondary minima and \(N - 2\) weak secondary maxima.

cards.title: Line width and dispersion
cards.body: The angular half-width of the \(m\)th principal maximum is \(\Delta\theta_m = \lambda/(Nd\cos\theta_m)\), becoming sharper as \(N\) grows. Angular dispersive power is \(\Delta\theta/\Delta\lambda = m/(d\cos\theta)\).

cards.title: Resolving power of a grating
cards.body: By the Rayleigh criterion, two wavelengths \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda + \Delta\lambda\) are just resolved when the \(m\)th peak of one falls on the first adjacent minimum of the other: \(R = \lambda/\Delta\lambda = mN\).

cards.title: Resolving power R = mN
cards.legend: \(d\) grating element, \(\theta\) common diffraction angle, \(m\) order, \(N\) total ruled lines.

ask.q: How do we simplify the equation \(m\lambda + m\Delta\lambda = m\lambda + \lambda/N\)?
ask.why: Subtracting \(m\lambda\) cancels the common term on both sides.

steps.note: The \(m\lambda\) terms cancel on both sides.

ask.q: How do we rearrange \(m\Delta\lambda = \lambda/N\) to obtain the resolving power \(\lambda/\Delta\lambda\)?
ask.why: Multiplying both sides by \(N/\Delta\lambda\) brings \(mN\) to the left and \(\lambda/\Delta\lambda\) to the right.

steps.note: Isolate the ratio \(\lambda/\Delta\lambda\).

steps.note: Resolving power \(R = \lambda/\Delta\lambda\) equals order \(m\) times number of lines \(N\).

cards.label: Example
cards.title: Grating orders and resolution
cards.body: A \(15000\ \text{lines/inch}\) grating illuminated by \(\lambda = 600\ \text{nm}\) shows up to 2nd order (\(m_{max} = 2\)) and has 2nd-order resolving power \(R = 2 \times 15000 = 30000\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In the diffraction pattern of an N-slit grating, how many secondary minima lie between two adjacent principal maxima?
cards.why: Between \(\gamma = 0\) and \(\gamma = \pi\), \(\sin(N\gamma) = 0\) at \(\gamma = p\pi/N\) for \(p = 1, 2, \dots, N-1\), giving \(N - 1\) secondary minima.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: How does the angular dispersion \(\Delta\theta/\Delta\lambda\) of a diffraction grating depend on the grating element d?
cards.why: Differentiating \(d\sin\theta = m\lambda\) gives \(\Delta\theta/\Delta\lambda = m/(d\cos\theta)\), so a smaller \(d\) produces larger angular dispersion.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: What is the minimum number of grating lines N required to just resolve the sodium doublet (\(\lambda \approx 5890\ \text{\AA}\), \(\Delta\lambda = 5.89\ \text{\AA}\)) in the first order (\(m = 1\))?
cards.why: From \(R = \lambda/\Delta\lambda = mN\), for \(m = 1\) we need \(N = 5890 / 5.89 = 1000\) lines.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: Calculate the resolving power of a grating having \(5000\) lines in the third-order spectrum (\(m = 3\)).
cards.why: Resolving power is \(R = mN = 3 \times 5000 = 15000\).

cards.title: Schuster summation & Poisson spot
cards.body: Adjacent zones have opposite phases: \(u(P) = u_1 - u_2 + u_3 - u_4 + \dots \approx u_1/2\). If a circular disc blocks the first \(p\) zones, \(u(P) \approx u_{p+1}/2\), forming the bright Poisson spot.

cards.title: Fresnel zone plate
cards.body: A zone plate has concentric circles of radii \(r_n = K\sqrt{n}\) with alternate zones blackened. Blocking even (or odd) zones makes all transmitted zones add in phase: \(u = u_1 + u_3 + u_5 + \dots\)

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: If a plane wave of intensity \(I_0\) falls on a circular aperture whose radius equals the radius of the first Fresnel half-period zone, what is the axial intensity at P?
cards.why: The unobstructed wavefront produces amplitude \(u_0 = u_1/2\). Letting through only the first zone gives amplitude \(u_1 = 2u_0\), so intensity is \(4I_0\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: How does the principal focal length \(f = r_1^2/\lambda\) of a Fresnel zone plate depend on wavelength \(\lambda\)?
options: Inversely proportional to \(\lambda\), showing strong chromatic aberration
cards.why: Since \(f = r_1^2/\lambda\), violet light focuses farther from the zone plate than red light, producing strong chromatic aberration.

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: The bright spot always formed at the centre of the shadow of an opaque circular disc is known as the ______ spot.
cards.why: Poisson predicted from Fresnel's wave theory that an opaque disc obstructing \(p\) zones leaves amplitude \(u_{p+1}/2\) on the axis, creating a central bright spot.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: A zone plate has its first ring of radius \(r_1 = 1\ \text{mm}\) and is illuminated by a plane wave of wavelength \(500\ \text{nm}\). Find its principal focal length in metres.
cards.why: The principal focal length is \(f = r_1^2/\lambda = (10^{-3}\ \text{m})^2 / (5 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{m}) = 2\ \text{m}\).

cards.title: Fresnel integrals & Cornu's spiral
cards.body: Straight-edge diffraction uses the Fresnel integrals \(C(\tau) = \int_0^\tau \cos(\pi u^2/2)du\) and \(S(\tau) = \int_0^\tau \sin(\pi u^2/2)du\). Their parametric plot is Cornu's spiral.

cards.title: Straight-edge intensity law
cards.body: At height \(y\) above the geometrical shadow edge (at distance \(d\)), setting \(v_0 = -\sqrt{2/(\lambda d)}\,y\) gives \(I(P) = \frac{1}{2}I_0\{[\frac{1}{2} - C(v_0)]^2 + [\frac{1}{2} - S(v_0)]^2\}\).

cards.title: Shadow vs illuminated region
cards.body: On the shadow edge (\(y = 0\)), intensity is \(I_0/4\). Inside the shadow (\(y < 0\)), \(I\) falls monotonically to zero; in the lit region (\(y > 0\)), \(I\) oscillates with diminishing amplitude about \(I_0\).

ask.why: Since \(y = 0\) lies on the line of the geometrical shadow edge, \(v_0 = 0\).

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: In Fresnel diffraction at a straight edge, how does the intensity behave as the observation point moves deep into the geometrical shadow?
options: It decreases monotonically to zero without oscillating
It oscillates with maxima and minima of equal spacing
It rises to a central Poisson bright fringe
cards.why: As \(y \to -\infty\) (\(v_0 \to +\infty\)), the point on Cornu's spiral approaches \((1/2, 1/2)\) smoothly, so the chord length and intensity decrease monotonically to zero.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: What are the asymptotic values of the Fresnel integrals \(C(\infty)\) and \(S(\infty)\)?
cards.why: Using \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{i\pi u^2/2}du = 1 + i = 2[C(\infty) + iS(\infty)]\), we get \(C(\infty) = S(\infty) = 1/2\).

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: The parametric plot of the Fresnel integrals \(C(\tau)\) and \(S(\tau)\) used to analyse Fresnel diffraction is called ______ spiral.
cards.why: Marie Cornu introduced the parametric curve of \(S(\tau)\) versus \(C(\tau)\), known as Cornu's spiral.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: A plane wave of unobstructed intensity \(I_0 = 80\ \text{W/m}^2\) is incident normally on a straight edge. What is the intensity right at the edge of the geometrical shadow?
cards.why: At the edge of the geometrical shadow (\(y = 0\)), the intensity is \(I = I_0 / 4 = 80 / 4 = 20\ \text{W/m}^2\).

cards.title: Linear & circular polarisation
cards.body: A wave propagating along \(z\) with displacement confined to a single plane (like \(E_x = E_0\cos(kz-\omega t), E_y = 0\)) is linearly polarised. Equal \(x,y\) components \(90^\circ\) out of phase give circular polarisation.

cards.title: Unpolarised light & transverse proof
cards.body: In unpolarised light, the transverse electric vector changes direction randomly every ~\(10^{-8}\ \text{s}\). Extinguishing light by rotating a second Polaroid (analyser) proves light is a transverse wave.

cards.title: Malus' law
cards.body: When linearly polarised light of amplitude \(E_0\) (intensity \(I_0\)) hits an analyser whose pass-axis is at angle \(\theta\) to \(\mathbf{E}\), transmitted amplitude is \(E_0\cos\theta\) and intensity is \(I = I_0\cos^2\theta\).

cards.title: Wire grid and Polaroid
cards.body: In a wire grid or iodine-doped polymer Polaroid, the \(\mathbf{E}\) component parallel to the conducting wires/chains drives electrons and is absorbed as Joule heat; the perpendicular component passes through.

cards.title: Polaroids at 45° and 60°
cards.body: Rotating the analyser from \(0^\circ\) to \(45^\circ\) halves the transmitted intensity; at \(60^\circ\) it drops to \(25\%\), and at \(90^\circ\) it vanishes.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: When an unpolarised electromagnetic wave falls on a wire-grid polariser, which component of the electric field is transmitted?
options: The component perpendicular to the wires
The component parallel to the wires
Only the longitudinal component along the wave vector
cards.why: The electric field parallel to the wires drives conduction currents and is absorbed as Joule heat, so the perpendicular component is transmitted.

cards.label: Quiz · OMR
cards.q: For a circularly polarised wave propagating along the z-axis with \(x = a\cos(kz - \omega t + \phi)\), what is the corresponding y-displacement?
cards.why: A \(90^\circ\) phase difference between equal \(x\) and \(y\) components gives \(x^2 + y^2 = a^2\), tracing a circle.

cards.label: Quiz · Fill in
cards.q: The phenomenon of polarisation proves that light waves are ______ in nature.
cards.why: Longitudinal waves have displacement along the direction of propagation and cannot show intensity variation when a slit or polariser is rotated.

cards.label: Quiz · Number
cards.q: A linearly polarised beam of intensity \(40\ \text{W/m}^2\) is incident on an analyser whose pass-axis makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the electric vector. Find the transmitted intensity.
cards.why: By Malus' law, \(I = I_0 \cos^2 60^\circ = 40 \times (0.5)^2 = 10\ \text{W/m}^2\).
